# Errors

Every I/O method returns `(T, error)` (Go's idiomatic error model). A
non-nil error is either a transport failure or a non-2xx response after
the network layer's retries (exponential backoff + jitter, `401`
refresh, `Retry-After`). A non-2xx response is a
`*gantryruntime.APIError` carrying the HTTP `Status`, Box's error `Code`,
`Message`, and `RequestID`, the response `Header`, and the raw `Body`:

```go
var apiErr *gantryruntime.APIError
if errors.As(err, &apiErr) && apiErr.Status == http.StatusNotFound {
	// apiErr.Code == "not_found"; quote apiErr.RequestID to Box support
}
```

## Etags: `If-None-Match` and `If-Match`

Files and folders carry an `etag`. Send it back to stay in sync with Box
(Box's [Ensure consistency](https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/ensure-consistency/)
guide):

- **Reads** — a file, folder, or web link `get`, and each shared-item lookup, has an
  `…IfModified` variant that takes the stored etag, sends it as
  `If-None-Match`, and returns `nil, nil` when Box answers `304 Not Modified`:
  keep your cached copy. (The plain method surfaces that 304 as the error
  above if you set `if-none-match` on it yourself.)
- **Writes** — pass the etag as `IfMatch` on a file, folder, or web link update or
  delete, or a new file version upload. Box answers `412 Precondition
  Failed` (code `precondition_failed`) when the item changed since you read
  it, and `gantryruntime.IsPreconditionFailed(err)` reports it: read it
  again, reapply your change, retry. `If-Match` can't block a move.

```go
file, err := client.Files.GetIfModified(ctx, fileID, etag, nil)
if err == nil && file == nil {
	// unchanged since etag
}

// Re-read and retry: the update lands only on the version it was made from.
for attempt := 1; ; attempt++ {
	_, err = client.Files.Update(ctx, fileID, body, &managers.FilesUpdateOptions{IfMatch: &etag})
	if !gantryruntime.IsPreconditionFailed(err) || attempt == 3 {
		break
	}
	current, err := client.Files.Get(ctx, fileID, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	etag = current.Etag.Value // reapply your change to current here
}
```
